Keyword reference

Every Faber keyword, primitive type, and intrinsic has one canonical (Latin) name and one spelling per reader pack. This page is the full join across all eight packs, so a term can be translated by reading across a row.

The tables are generated from the packs themselves and cannot drift from the compiler by hand. A blank cell is a pack that declares no spelling for that term — the contested rows are listed at the end rather than filled in.

How to read a table#

  • Across a row translates one term into any of the eight surfaces.
  • Down a column is the vocabulary one locale writes Faber in.
  • The la column is the canonical name, which is also the compiler's internal identity. It is one locale among eight, not a privileged one: rendering to English and rendering to Thai are the same operation.

Arabic is right-to-left; its column runs in logical order inside this left-to-right block, so the characters read correctly even though the row places them among Latin script.

The eight installed packs, in the column order used below:

CodeNative nameScriptDirection
enEnglishLatinleft-to-right
laLatinaLatinleft-to-right
arالعربيةArabicright-to-left
hiहिन्दीDevanagarileft-to-right
th-THไทยThaileft-to-right
viTiếng ViệtLatin (Vietnamese)left-to-right
zh-Hans简体中文Han (Simplified)left-to-right
zh-Hant繁體中文Han (Traditional)left-to-right
